newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes mixed, Tapis paper down in catch-up.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes mixed, Tapis paper down in catch-up.

text.p: Asian crude prices were mixed on Tuesday, with Middle East grades gaining from futures rebound, but regional grades catching up with last week's futures losses.
SIMEX March Brent last traded at $21.20 per barrel, up seven cents from London, which hit a five-month low last week of $20.55.
March Tapis paper was quoted at $21.80/$22.10 in Singapore on Tuesday, down from around $23.00 late last week before the long holiday weekend when markets were closed Friday and Monday.
That drove outright prices lower on regional grades, although some players were reporting some premium strength for light sweet crude.
One producer has sold its March Kutubu, Cossack and Griffin grades for more than Tapis quotes plus 25 cents, traders said, after pockets of demand emerged.
None of the barrels went into Australia, which could prompt some further demand for light sweet grades, market sources said.
One player said there was still some demand from South Korea and Japan for light sweet oil, despite an expected weakness in these grades as seasonal demand wanes for middle distillates.

The latest Tapis deals by a producer were widely talked in the market, although some players said the structure of the latest cargo done into New Zealand may have had special conditions attached, which supported a premium of more than $1.30.

News of late trading in March MidEast crude emerged, with some Murban, Oman and possibly Lower Zakum changing hands late last week at premiums no higher than plus five cents, a reflection of a seasonally weaker market.
